Haraḥaman for all humankind and all living creatures following the Sefirat haOmer, by Jonathan Schachter

tei:bibl.tei:title: הָרַחֲמָן לְכָל אָדָם וְהמְרַחֵם עַל־הַבְּרִיּוֹת
Haraḥaman for all humankind and all living creatures following the Sefirat haOmer, by Jonathan Schachter
tei:bibl.tei:author: Jonathan Schachter
tei:bibl.tei:note: Converted from the export of opensiddur.org at 624215eef0.

tei:div.tei:p: The following brief prayer may be said, immediately following the Omer count, by those who find it difficult or problematic to simply ask for a return to the days of animal sacrifice in the Beit HaMiqdash, and who long for reconciliation, sensitivity and peaceful coexistence between and among all Jews and the other Peoples of the Earth (as well as all living creatures!), as envisioned by the Prophets.

This “Haraḥaman” prayer by Jonathan Schachter was composed during the Sefirat haOmer period in 5785 (2025), as an alternative to the familiar haraḥaman for the restoration of the ancient mode of Temple worship that is said following the count.
